author: Nelev
body:
## Summary

- **The agent reads the caller's record.** `search_patient_record` searched the constant `RECORD_ID`, so every signed-in user — every new account since #34 — was answered from the seeded patient's record. `/ask` now passes `record_id(user_id)` (`pat_{users.id}`, the convention `agent/patient.py` owns) to `answer()`.
- **The model still can't choose the record.** `answer()` hands the ID to the run as LangChain runtime context (`context_schema=RecordContext`, `ainvoke(..., context=...)`). The tool reads it from its injected `ToolRuntime`, which LangChain leaves out of the tool schema — `query` remains the only argument the model can set.
- **Forgetting it fails loudly.** `record_id` is keyword-only with no default.
- **README**: the RAG section says where the record comes from; the "hardcoded record" known gap is removed.

## Behaviour after merge

The seeded patient keeps being answered from their record. An account with no indexed record gets no passages, and the model says the record shows nothing relevant.

## Test plan

- [x] `ruff check`, `ruff format` on changed files, `pytest` — 114 pass (was 109)
  - `/ask` passes `pat_{USER_ID}` on both paths (new conversation, follow-up)
  - `tests/test_agent.py`: the tool schema exposes only `query`; the tool searches the context's record; `answer()` passes `RecordContext(record_id)` to the graph
- [x] The real `create_agent` graph, driven by a scripted fake model that calls the tool: LangChain injected the run's context and `search_record` received `pat_abc`
- [x] Production `build_agent()` compiles with the new `context_schema`
- [ ] Ask a question as the seeded patient and as a new account
